rules.name: C self-assignment

message.text: this assignment writes an initialized C local back to itself

rules.description: A plain C assignment to a direct ordinary primitive scalar local has a whole bare-identifier right-hand side resolving to the same binding. The right-hand read has one exact prior reaching definition on every path, and the prepared syntax, binding, reaching, and same-evaluation evidence is exhaustive. Unsupported storage, syntax, preprocessing, and flow cases remain open instead of becoming findings.

rules.name: Fixed conditional outcome

message.text: this condition has a fixed truth value under the proven scalar constraints

rules.description: One outcome of this exact condition is impossible under the proven scalar facts at its decision point, so either its true arm or its false arm cannot run. The row orientation records which outcome is impossible. The proof accounts for the control-flow path that reaches the condition; unsupported predicates, partial semantic evidence, and inexact source mappings remain inconclusive. Review the intended condition and branch behavior before changing code.

rules.name: Discarded pure transformation result

message.text: the result of this reviewed pure String transformation is discarded

rules.description: The exact JDK 21 String.trim() return value is unused by an expression statement or for-loop initializer/update. Expression lambdas remain incomplete until their functional return contract is proven. This diagnostic requires a reviewed pure-transformation obligation, exact result-use syntax, a selected JDK source artifact, and complete dispatch coverage. Calls with missing model or artifact evidence remain incomplete.

rules.name: Dynamic code evaluation

message.text: Replace dynamic evaluation with explicit parsing or dispatch

rules.description: Calls that evaluate source text as code are difficult to validate and can execute unintended behavior. Prefer a data-only representation and explicit operations.

rules.name: Empty failure handler

message.text: this catch body contains no failure-handling statements

rules.description: An exact Java catch clause has no non-comment body statements. This is a structural review finding: it does not establish that the catch is reachable or that its exception type can be thrown. Recovered or unavailable syntax is inconclusive. Review whether the exception needs handling or propagation; comments do not count as handling. No automatic fix is supplied.

rules.name: Failed local swap

message.text: the second assignment copies back the first assignment's value

rules.description: Two adjacent ordinary local assignments have crossed exact binding identities: a = b followed by b = a. Exact reaching evidence proves the second read receives the first write, which can indicate a failed swap. Intent is not inferred and no automatic fix is offered.

rules.name: Go data race

message.text: these exact accesses to the same Go location may execute concurrently without ordering or compatible protection

rules.description: Two ordinary Go memory accesses identify the same exact runtime location, at least one writes, their task instances may execute concurrently, and no modeled happens-before edge, compatible must-held lock, or all-atomic access pair protects them. Findings require proven and exhaustive workspace evidence; unresolved or unsupported concurrency remains open.

rules.name: Go nil dereference

message.text: this Go operation may dereference a nil value on a reachable path

rules.description: A structured pointer dereference, field access, or reviewed receiver operation is reached with an exact Nil or MaybeNil fact. Reviewed API result contracts are also retained as a nilness origin when an operation requiring a valid result occurs before its success condition is proved. Unknown scalar facts, nil-tolerant methods, and unreviewed receiver operations are not findings.

rules.name: Go failure path returns the wrong error

message.text: this exact Go API failure path returns a call that consumes a different error binding whose reaching value is nil

rules.description: A reviewed Go API reports failure through one result, but a call returned from that exact failure path consumes a different error binding whose reaching value is proven to be Go's zero value. The rule does not infer intent from names: it requires canonical API identity, exact result and binding identity, exact failure-edge control, and exhaustive reaching-definition evidence.

rules.name: Identical conditional branches

message.text: two branches of this conditional have equivalent bodies under proven reference identities

rules.description: Two arms of the same ordered conditional have equivalent structured bodies under proven reference identities. This may be a copy/paste error or redundant control flow. Inspect the condition and branch intent; removing the conditional requires preserving condition evaluation, bindings, and scope. Ordinary local or parameter references and calls through the same lexical callee binding qualify. Java fields and calls qualify only with one exact indexed target, equivalent receivers, and equivalent arguments. Unresolved or ambiguous callees, other property operations, and unresolved binding identities remain open.

rules.name: Ignored file-deletion status

message.text: the reviewed deletion status is discarded

rules.description: The exact JDK 21 Files.deleteIfExists(Path) call returns a Boolean status: false means no file was deleted because it did not exist. An expression statement or for-loop initializer/update discards that status. Expression lambdas require a resolved functional return contract. I/O exceptions remain separate. This diagnostic requires exact selected-artifact and dispatch evidence; it does not claim that discarding the status is always a bug.

rules.name: Local self-assignment

message.text: this assignment writes an initialized local back to itself

rules.description: A direct assignment reads and writes the same ordinary local binding. Prepared syntax and procedure-local reaching evidence prove the right-hand read was initialized and the assignment has no indirect target or effectful right-hand expression.

rules.name: Loop body never repeats

message.text: this loop body cannot reach its next iteration

rules.description: The exact Java loop body is reachable, but every modeled continuation leaves before its own repeat edge. An intentional do-while(false) is excluded. Review the loop structure and early exits before changing code; no automatic rewrite is supplied.

rules.name: Overwritten unread local value

message.text: the local value is overwritten before it is read

rules.description: An exact ordinary local establishment is replaced on every modeled continuation before any read of that value. The row retains every first replacement event as evidence. Review the original assignment and its right-hand-side effects; no automatic removal is offered.

rules.name: Python absent member

message.text: this Python receiver may hold a proven class that does not declare the accessed member

rules.description: Caller-driven class-set propagation proves that a reachable receiver can hold a class whose complete modeled surface lacks the accessed member. Partial receiver sets, unresolved hierarchies, dynamic attribute hooks, and incomplete member models do not produce findings. A clean run means no Proven absence was found, not that all runtime receivers were classified. Missing Python declaration-model coverage makes the run inconclusive.

rules.name: Rayon parallelism inside a blocking lazy initializer

message.text: Review this blocking lazy initializer: its rayon parallelism can self-deadlock when the first call arrives on a rayon worker

rules.description: A blocking lazy-init primitive (OnceLock::get_or_init, OnceLock::get_or_try_init, Once::call_once, LazyLock::new) whose initializer closure lexically contains rayon parallelism (par_iter, into_par_iter, par_bridge, par_chunks) can self-deadlock: when the first initialization runs on a rayon worker, the initializer's parallel join steals sibling jobs, and a stolen job that re-enters the same cell parks on it forever. This is a structural review prompt, not proof of a deadlock; verify whether the cell can be reached from inside a rayon pool. Containment is lexical: a rayon call inside a nested closure defined within the initializer also matches, even when that closure only runs later. Bare rayon::join, rayon::scope, and ThreadPool::install are not matched because their unqualified names are too generic. Prefer a pool-safe memoization such as PoolSafeMemo::get_or_build_parallel, or build the value eagerly before entering the parallel region.

rules.name: Redundant Boolean return branches

message.text: the conditional paths return complementary Boolean literals

rules.description: The conditional's two immediate paths return opposite Boolean literals with no intervening work. The second path is an else arm or an adjacent return in the same block. The relation records whether the true path returns true or false. Review the intended result; no automatic replacement with the condition is implied because truthiness, conversions, and condition effects require separate proof.

rules.name: Repeated stable branch condition

message.text: this later branch repeats an earlier condition whose tested values cannot have changed

rules.description: A later condition in one ordered if/else-if chain repeats an earlier condition over the same ordinary bindings. Each intervening condition is proven effect free, so the later branch cannot be selected. Calls, getters, Python truthiness hooks, and unresolved bindings are not proof of stability. Review the intended alternative test; no automatic fix is implied.

rules.name: Resource lifecycle

message.text: Resource can leave its analysis root without being closed

rules.description: Reports a resource acquired by a supported acquisition family that reaches a normal or exceptional analysis-root exit without a supported close. Unsupported escape, ownership-transfer, and alias shapes stay inconclusive instead of clean.

rules.name: Unreachable statement

message.text: this statement cannot execute

rules.description: Every producer-authored entry to this exact Java statement is outside the complete bounded control-flow region reachable from the procedure entry. Missing statement entries, unknown control, source mismatch, cancellation, and budget exhaustion remain inconclusive. Review the preceding flow and intended statement before removing code.

rules.name: Unsafe object deserialization

message.text: Replace pickle deserialization with a data-only format

rules.description: Python pickle loaders may instantiate unexpected objects. Prefer a data-only format and validate the decoded schema.

rules.name: Database call inside a loop

message.text: Review whether this lexically nested database call repeats per iteration

rules.description: A database call lexically nested under a loop can signal an N+1 pattern. This structural prompt also includes deferred nested bodies; verify execution before batching or prefetching. A for-each loop whose iterated expression provably resolves to a collection literal with at most eight elements is excluded; the proof covers declarator-established bindings (JS/TS const/let/var, Rust let, Java locals), so field-, assignment-, or call-produced iterables still report.

rules.name: Expensive operation inside nested loops

message.text: Review whether this lexically nested operation repeats across both loops

rules.description: This operation is lexically nested under two loops. The structural prompt also includes deferred nested bodies; verify execution before hoisting invariants, batching work, or reducing the iteration space. The prompt is withdrawn when the inner for-each loop's iterated expression provably resolves to a collection literal with at most eight elements, because a fixed small inner dimension makes the work linear in the outer loop rather than multiplicative; the proof covers declarator-established bindings (JS/TS const/let/var, Rust let, Java locals), so field-, assignment-, or call-produced iterables still report.

rules.name: File read inside a loop

message.text: Review whether this lexically nested file read repeats per iteration

rules.description: A file-read call lexically nested under a loop may multiply I/O and allocation. This structural prompt also includes deferred nested bodies; verify execution before reading once, streaming, or batching. A for-each loop whose iterated expression provably resolves to a collection literal with at most eight elements is excluded; the proof covers declarator-established bindings (JS/TS const/let/var, Rust let, Java locals), so field-, assignment-, or call-produced iterables still report.

rules.name: Loop-invariant receiver sorted on every iteration

message.text: this receiver's value is established outside the enclosing loop and never re-established inside it, so every iteration re-sorts the same value; if the call sits in a closure or other deferred body, it is reported because it is written inside the loop, not because it is proven to run once per iteration

rules.description: The sorted receiver's value is established outside the enclosing loop -- its binding is declared outside and no assignment inside the loop reaches that binding -- so the loop re-sorts one unchanged-identity value on every pass. Sort once before the loop, or maintain order incrementally. Receivers that are field projections of another value are outside this rule's evidence and are not reported either way.

rules.name: Network request inside a loop

message.text: Review whether this lexically nested network request repeats per iteration

rules.description: A network call lexically nested under a loop may amplify latency and remote load. This structural prompt also includes deferred nested bodies; verify execution before batching or adding bounded concurrency. A for-each loop whose iterated expression provably resolves to a collection literal with at most eight elements is excluded; the proof covers declarator-established bindings (JS/TS const/let/var, Rust let, Java locals), so field-, assignment-, or call-produced iterables still report.

rules.name: Parsing inside a loop

message.text: Review whether this lexically nested parse repeats invariant work

rules.description: A parse call lexically nested under a loop may repeat tokenization, validation, and allocation. This structural prompt also includes deferred nested bodies; verify execution and invariance before hoisting it. A for-each loop whose iterated expression provably resolves to a collection literal with at most eight elements is excluded; the proof covers declarator-established bindings (JS/TS const/let/var, Rust let, Java locals), so field-, assignment-, or call-produced iterables still report.

rules.name: Regular-expression compilation inside a loop

message.text: Review whether this lexically nested regex compilation repeats per iteration

rules.description: Regex compilation lexically nested under a loop may rebuild parser and matcher state. This structural prompt also includes deferred nested bodies; verify execution and invariance before hoisting it. A for-each loop whose iterated expression provably resolves to a collection literal with at most eight elements is excluded; the proof covers declarator-established bindings (JS/TS const/let/var, Rust let, Java locals), so field-, assignment-, or call-produced iterables still report.

rules.name: Serialization inside a loop

message.text: Review whether this lexically nested serialization repeats per iteration

rules.description: Serialization lexically nested under a loop may repeat traversal, encoding, and allocation. This structural prompt also includes deferred nested bodies; verify execution before hoisting or batching. A for-each loop whose iterated expression provably resolves to a collection literal with at most eight elements is excluded; the proof covers declarator-established bindings (JS/TS const/let/var, Rust let, Java locals), so field-, assignment-, or call-produced iterables still report.

rules.name: Sleep inside a collection-iteration loop

message.text: Review whether this sleep throttles every iterated item

rules.description: A sleep call lexically nested under a for-each loop delays every iterated item, which can signal lockstep throttling of a whole batch. Condition-controlled while loops are excluded: a sleep there is usually the deliberate mechanism of a poll or bounded-backoff loop. This structural prompt also includes deferred nested bodies; verify execution before restructuring. A for-each loop whose iterated expression provably resolves to a collection literal with at most eight elements is also excluded; the proof covers declarator-established bindings (JS/TS const/let/var, Rust let, Java locals), so field-, assignment-, or call-produced iterables still report.

rules.name: Subprocess creation inside a loop

message.text: Review whether this lexically nested subprocess launch repeats per iteration

rules.description: A subprocess call lexically nested under a loop may repeat expensive process creation. This structural prompt also includes deferred nested bodies; verify execution before reusing a process or batching input. A for-each loop whose iterated expression provably resolves to a collection literal with at most eight elements is excluded; the proof covers declarator-established bindings (JS/TS const/let/var, Rust let, Java locals), so field-, assignment-, or call-produced iterables still report.

rules.name: Servlet parameter reaches JDBC SQL

message.text: A servlet request parameter reached the SQL text of Statement.execute(String)

rules.description: Reports attacker-controlled ServletRequest.getParameter(String) values that reach the SQL argument of the exact JDBC Statement.execute(String) overload. The rule does not treat PreparedStatement value binding or unrelated same-named APIs as SQL structure sinks.

rules.name: Environment variable reaches Runtime.exec

message.text: An environment variable reached the command argument of Runtime.exec(String)

rules.description: Reports values returned by the exact System.getenv(String) overload that reach the command argument of the exact Runtime.exec(String) overload. The rule excludes Runtime.exec(String[]) and unrelated same-named APIs.

rules.name: Process input reaches os.system

message.text: A process input reached the command argument of os.system(command)

rules.description: Reports values read from the CPython process environment (os.environ) or the launch argument vector (sys.argv) that reach the command argument of os.system. The command runs in a subshell, so attacker-controlled text in it changes the executed command. Source identity is the import binder plus the reviewed process-input model, never the spelling of a name; sink identity is the exact reviewed os.system member.
